Name: Better Balance - Custom Prices and Extra Features for Fairer Choices
Author: Xen0nex
Description:
[center][size=5][b]This mod is for:[/b][/size][/center]
[b]Casual Players[/b] wanting more paths to be viable or to feel less harshly "punished" for not picking the optimal "meta" choices, [b]Experienced Players[/b] seeking to extend the mid-game before they are able to easily buy all the end-game items, [b]Min-Maxers[/b] who want more variety among the optimal choices depending on circumstances, or [b]Longtime Players[/b] looking to re-experience the process of trying out a variety of unknown choices and working out which ones work best with their playstyle on their own.


[center][b][size=5]Goals of this mod:[/size][/b][/center]

I used spreadsheets to simulate a variety of scenarios and carefully adjusted the prices of most crops, seeds, animal products, animals, and a few other details while changing as little else as possible to maximize compatibility with other mods. With these adjusted item prices, this mod aims to:

[spoiler][list]
[*]Slow the exponential growth / income snowballing in Year 1 a bit, to force experienced players to spend more time playing with non-optimal "in Progress" farms at various stages of efficiency, instead of jumping right to optimized maximum production farms after just a season or two.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Reduce [b]maximum[/b] income substantially, to make the end-game expensive gold-sink items harder to get right away for experienced players.  (Max outdoor crop or Greenhouse per-tile profits are only ~40% of Vanilla, and max animal(pig) profits are ~30%)[/*]
[/list]
﻿(A side effect of the above 2 points should be that while I haven't changed them much in this mod, non-farm activities such as Fishing / Mining / Foraging / Fish Ponds should stay worthwhile for longer before farming overtakes them, and won't ever fall quite so far behind as they do in Vanilla) 

[list]
[*]Generally raise the [b]minimum[/b] income by buffing all of the low-performance options, so that even a player who is always making the "worst" choices can still typically expect to at least make a reasonable income. In fact, on average most crops have increased value with [i]Better Balance[/i].[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make Animals be a viable alternative to Crops for gold/day/tile, at all stages of development.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make Shepherd & Coopmaster increase maximum possible yields from Barns & Coops more than Artisan does, if using the appropriate animals & playstyles.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make the best Barns / Coops with Shepherd / Coopmaster give gold/day/tile on par or better than the best outdoor crops with Artisan, as Barns & Coops require more starting gold/time investment and more initial daily care to reach the maximum, and cannot "snowball" as fast as crops due to construction waiting times.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make selling Coop animals worthwhile, and an integral part of what makes Coopmaster Coops so profitable.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]To make Barns and Coops distinct, have Coops generally give better gold/day/tile, but Barns generally give both better total gold per Barn/Coop, and better gold/day/tile/interaction.  (Essentially, Barns require fewer animals to look after to reach the same profits as Coops.)  Taking Coopmaster / Shepherd can change this, however.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]To make the "higher tier" animals generally more profitable than the "starter" ones, at least with the right playstyle and / or profession.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]To make the average profitability of the seasons for crops go from Spring to Summer to Fall in increasing profits, as in-game text implies should be the case (in fact, Fall crops generally are now significantly more valuable than in vanilla).  Winter Seeds remain an option, but with the lowest profitability of all seasons.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Reduce the huge gulf in difference between the high-profit crops (& animals) and the lower profit ones, so that most choices are a bit closer to the average profitability for that season/building.  Even for "casual" players, this should help "low-performance" choices feel less unfairly punishing, and "high-performance" choices feel less arbitrarily powerful. E.G. While the "best" crops for a season in vanilla can be up to 5x or 10x more profitable than the "worst" ones, in [i]Better Balance[/i] the biggest the difference gets is about 2x, and which crop is the "worst" often varies depending on the circumstances.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Relatedly, instead of 1~2 crops/animals from each season being clearly optimal in all situations, have the "top" option vary depending on circumstances, to allow most crops (& animals) have at least some reasonable scenario, context, or playstyle where they could arguably be considered the "best" choice.  Thus, the highest gold/day crop for a given season will often change based on factors such as which tier of fertilizer you are using, or having Artisan or not, or how many kegs vs. jars you have available, or how much cash on hand you have available, or how much daily interactions you are willing to do, or even which Farm Map you chose.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]To very roughly introduce a trend where all else being equal, options which require many interactions per week often tend to yield better profits than options which only require few interactions per week (with exceptions).[/*]
[/list]
(As an example of the above 3 points, now instead of being the best crop to plant outdoors, Ancient Fruit will usually give a little less profit than planting "optimal" crops in that space all year, but still has the advantage of needing comparatively less maintenance / kegs / planning)

[list]
[*]To make buying the higher value Fruit Trees less of a "no-brainer" choice against the lower value ones.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Relatedly, make buying the higher value Fruit Trees more of a long term investment taking multiple seasons of produce to pay off.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make Honey a viable alternative to crops / animals, and make Green Tea more worthwhile.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Make tapping trees for syrups to sell more competitive with other options like crops, honey, etc.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Give more variety to the choice of tree type or layout when making mushroom log farms, depending on factors such as having the Tapper/Artisan professions, using Dehydrators/Preserves Jars, etc.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make a few more situations where Preserves Jars might be chosen over Kegs late-game.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make the gap between Artisan and Agriculturist smaller, with some situations where Agriculturist gives better profit.[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Make it easy for users to tweak & adjust all of the prices changes this mod makes (and more).[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[center][size=5][b]Optional Features:[/b][/size][/center]

Alongside rebalancing the value of farm produce & food and allowing the user to optionally further customize their prices, to reach the goals detailed above Better Balance also makes various other balancing adjustments to certain things which have a big impact on farm profits. These optional features are all enabled by default (with one exception, as enabling it on a existing save can have a surprising effect if you weren't expecting it), but can be individually disabled or configured in the two [b]config.json[/b] files or ideally in-game through the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url]. These features include:

[spoiler][list]
[*]Making the Crystalarium take ~2.7x as long to clone most gems﻿ (1.35x as long for Quartz & Fire Quartz), to not overshadow the new balance of crops & animals while staying competitive.[/*]
[*]Making Casks age items twice as fast (i.e. Casks take half as many days to improve the quality of items), to bring them closer to the gold/day/tile profits of using the same time or Cellar space to grow & sell raw crops or hold machines to process more raw crops.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Adjusting the crafting recipes, production time, and/or recipe purchase price of certain powerful 1.6 machines such as Mushroom Logs or Fish Smokers. Mushroom Logs in particular are heavily nerfed since in vanilla they are by far the most profitable option, especially if you are also tapping the nearby trees.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Adjusting the crafting recipes of certain fertilizers[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Recategorizing Smoked Fish as Fish products instead of Artisan Goods, so that the Artisan profession no longer increases their value. Similarly, recategorizing Dino Eggs to not be Artifacts and thus not have their valued tripled with a certain Power which triples the value of all Artifacts.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Applying an additional modifier to the value of all Animal produce once certain late-game crackers become available, so that animals do not become immensely more profitable than crops at that point. This modifier can either be applied all at once or slowly over time at a configurable rate.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Allowing trading certain late game crackers for top tier fertilizers or raisins from Pierre, so that they might still be useful on farms not using many animals / fish ponds.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Reducing the purchase price for 2 extremely expensive end-game items, to partially balance out the lowered maximum profits possible in Better Balance.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Adjusting the multiplier for the purchase price of all items at Joja Mart, with or without a membership.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]([i]Better Balance C# config setting[/i]) Replacing "expensive" Fruit Tree Sapling rewards with the corresponding "cheap" varieties when redeeming Prize Tickets or opening certain geode-style items.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]([i]Better Balance C# config setting)[/i] Allowing certain late game crackers to also be earned with a very low chance when performing actions that grant Farming XP (such as harvesting crops/animal products or petting animals by hand/scythe), so that fishing is not the main way to earn them.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]([i]Better Balance C# config setting[/i]) Making certain late game crackers also increase the resale value of animals, so that they are still useful for animals you instead to raise & sell for profit, such as egg laying animals in "cycled" Coops, etc.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]([i]Better Balance C# config setting[/i]) Making animals give increased Farming XP  (through petting, milking, shearing, or collecting items off the floor in Coops) to better match the XP given by crops.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]([i]Better Balance C# config setting[/i]) Making animals give full Mastery points (through petting, milking, shearing, or collecting items off the floor in Coops) instead of the reduced 50% Mastery points that all Farming XP (such as harvesting crops) gives in Vanilla, since the amount of XP you can get from animals does not scale up nearly as quickly as the amount of XP you can get from harvesting crops.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]([i]Better Balance C# config setting, [/i][b]disabled by default[/b]) Making the Ginger Island Farm only able to grow crops / Fruit Tree fruit which are able to grow in Summer instead of crops/fruit from any season like the Greenhouse. This both fits better thematically (a tropical island should only support crops that can handle the high heat) and reduces how profitable the Ginger Island farm is, as now only the Valley farm (and Greenhouse/Garden Pots) can grow the more profitable Fall crops. ﻿Adjusts the list of crops growable from Mixed Seeds on Ginger Island or Gourmand Frog's crop requests to always be crops growable in Summer. This feature is disabled by default as enabling it causes all non-Summer crops on the Island farm to wither overnight, so I wanted players on existing saves to have some control over when they enable it.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[center][b][size=5]Further Reading:[/size][/b][/center]

The points above summarize all the big picture things this mod should accomplish.  The specific changes vs. Vanilla can be seen in the various files in the mod's assets folder such as [i]pricesBalanced.json[/i] or [i]shopPricesBalanced.json[/i].  Check out the "[b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/671]Individual Overviews[/url][/b]" article for charts showcasing the strengths & weaknesses of crops in typical scenarios, and brief written overviews for special cases & animals.  Or don't, if you want to keep it a surprise and recreate the "blind first playthrough" experience of working out which things work better in certain situations on your own.  The "[b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/670]Explanation & Background[/url][/b]" article is if you want to dive into some of the assumptions made while balancing, or the thinking behind the "how & why" for much of the changes. 
Be aware that the various articles may have some unmarked [b]references to some 1.5 content[/b] if you are avoiding [b]spoilers[/b], but all [b]1.6 spoilers[/b] are in a spoiler container at the bottom of "[b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/671]Individual Overviews[/url][/b]".  If you're especially curious, you can look through the spreadsheets I used for balancing the various aspects in the [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/8141?tab=files]Miscellaneous Files[/url][/b] section, which also shows the profit for various configurations of both modded or Vanilla items.  The crops sheets in particular are based on a modified version of the wonderful [url=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Hd7M6ITTDcdGbqGiTtgrp0vgXuJqLaCP2xJ3LaV8gbU/edit#gid=142621552]Stardew Valley Community Spreadsheet's[/url] Crop Income page, with various corrections and additions.  The [b]Recommended Mods & Optional Plugins[/b] section below is also highly recommended, optionally.


[center][size=5][b]Installation & Usage:[/b][/size][/center]
[list]
[*]Install the latest version of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url]﻿[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Install the latest version of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1915]Content Patcher[/url][/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*](Optional) Install the latest version of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url]﻿﻿[/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*]Download the zipped file, and unzip its full contents into your [b]Stardew Valley\Mods\[/b] folder.[/*]
[/list]
This mod should work as expected with the Vanilla "Profit Margin" settings, although doing so will affect the balance of/between items.
That's all you need to start using it, although there are some [b]Recommended Mods & Optional Plugins[/b] detailed in a section below.

Please note while this mod should work without any issues on an existing save file (see paragraph below), the full effects of the balancing changes will be most noticeable on a new save file.  I believe this mod shouldn't affect the save file, and should be safe to uninstall at any point.

For using with [b]existing saves[/b], note that while all newly generated/harvested items should have their prices adjusted accordingly, any existing items that are already in the player's inventory, or in chests, or have already been spawned by machines, animals, or on the ground as foragable items on the dawn of the in-game day you install this mod will still have the old Vanilla prices.  To fix existing items with old prices, put them in a chest and then bring a stack of 1 or more matching items with the correct new price, then pull the old items out of the chest so that they join the new items in the player's inventory, where they will convert to the new price. Or simply sell the old items with the old vanilla prices, either way any new items you acquire will come with the correct adjusted price.

If using the [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url][/b] mod to change the price of items mid-day by changing the setting from in-game, the same process above applies.

[center][/center]
[center][b][size=5]Customization:[/size][/b][/center]

The values in this mod are the result of many hours spent simulating the performance of different options, but all of this has been done according to my personal tastes for balance.  [b]Users can easily make any price adjustments[/b] by editing .json files in the [i]Better Balance\[CP] Better Balance\assets[/i] folder, which should have names & descriptions for the changes commented behind "//". In particular, [b]pricesBalanced.json[/b] contains the vast majority of all price changes, with changes specific to the Stardew Valley Expanded mod in [b]SVEPatch.json[/b]. 

Users can also make adjustments to the prices for any items (including items / crops from other mods, or ones already edited by [i]Better Balance[/i]) by adding them to the [b]customItems.json[/b] template file, which can be reused in future updates without having to redo it each time. (IE, the edits to an item in [b]customItems.json[/b] take precedence over the edits to the same item in [b]pricesBalanced.json[/b]) More details in the in-game config description and notes at the top of [b]customItems.json[/b].

There are also 2 config.json files, one in each of the "[b][CP] Better Balance[/b]" and "[b]Better Balance[/b]" folders. 
The descriptions for the effects of the different settings can be read in [b]content.json[/b] in the [i]Better Balance\[CP] Better Balance[/i] folder, or read in-game with additional notes & descriptions if using the highly recommended [b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url][/b] mod. Toggling some of the options mid-day can require reloading the save / sleeping through the night to take effect.

Aside from the various settings to disable individual adjustments, the config includes values to ﻿apply price multipliers to all items within certain categories: [b]Fish, Animal Products, Animal Resale, Crops, Farm Forage, Flowers & Honey, [/b]and [b]Cooked Foods[/b] (and a[b] Custom[/b] category that you can add items to yourself if you want). This allows you to broadly adjust the balance between different playstyles/aspects of the game quickly, without having to go adjust each item's price individually. Changing the prices mid-day with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]GMCM[/url] can still adjust pre-existing items by following the steps above in the "using with existing saves" section. Note that changing these multipliers will affect the profitability & balancing of all items within that category.


[center][b][size=5]Compatibility:[/size][/b][/center]

As a relatively simple Content Patcher mod with some extra C# functions, this mod should be fairly compatible with other mods, so long as they don't also specifically attempt to alter the prices of the same crops / seeds / animal products in [b]Data/Objects[/b], or the same animal prices / production times in [b]Data/FarmAnimals, [b]Data/[/b]Machines, [/b]or[b] [b]Data/[/b]Shops[/b].  (For example, [i]SVE[/i]'s custom "[b]Lower Profit Margins[/b]" setting overwrites many of [i]Better Balance[/i]'s changes) Mods which change other things in those files should probably be fine, as far as I'm aware.  This mod also dynamically alters the prices of several items in some shops, so other mods which attempt to change those same items may run into issues.

Though all the mods in the [b]Recommended Mods & Optional Plugins[/b] section seem to work fine together with this mod for me, they may have their own compatibility concerns to check if you're using them alongside other mods. 

Using this mod alongside mods which add new crops or animals should not cause any errors, however note that by default this mod only rebalances the Vanilla (& most [i]Stardew Valley Expanded[/i]) crops & animals, so any mod-added items might have noticeably higher (or lower) profitability than the Vanilla items (unless you adjust them yourself using [b]customItems.json[/b]).

[size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/3753]Stardew Valley Expanded[/url]﻿
(or the standalone [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/8149]Crafting & Construction from SVE[/url] mod)[/size]
Description:
[spoiler][b]NOTE:[/b] Currently, enabling SVE's custom "[b]Lower Profit Margins[/b]" option in the config overwrites many of [i]Better Balance[/i]'s price changes, so using both together is not recommended.

You've likely either already heard of [i]Stardew Valley Expanded[/i] ([i]SVE[/i]), or are currently using it, although I'd recommend giving it a look if you haven't.

Related to this mod, however, are the "[b]Balanced Crafting[/b]" and "[b]Harder Building Construction[/b]" options in its config.  Together, these generally make many useful items & buildings require more resources and/or money to craft or build, with special attention to many high-performance items like Kegs or Iridium Sprinklers requiring more.  However, some underperforming items like default Sprinklers have cheaper recipes to encourage their use in exchange.  Overall this goes a long way to solving the "exponential snowball" of Year 1, and I appreciate how many repeating recipes requiring both more Wood and Hardwood make the Lumberjack profession more appealing.  The increased costs & recipes feel fair, as if correcting oversights, rather than introducing tedium for the sake of it.
The full changes of these two options can be compared with Vanilla at the [i]SVE [/i]wiki pages for [url=https://stardew-valley-expanded.fandom.com/wiki/Balanced_Crafting]Balanced Crafting[/url] and for [url=https://stardew-valley-expanded.fandom.com/wiki/Harder_Building_Construction]Harder Building Construction[/url] (wiki may not be updated for 1.6 yet).

I always play with [i]SVE [/i]& these settings enabled, and so while you can certainly use this mod by itself, your experience will be closer to how I've tested it if you use them.  

If you are using [i]SVE[/i], by default [i]Better Balance[/i] will adjust the price & value of [i]SVE [/i]crops, and the price bonuses you receive from various NPC events to be more in line with prices in [i]Better Balance[/i] (can be toggled in the config).  You can see the exact changes to the bonuses at [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/8141?tab=docs]the bottom of the readme document[/url]. Aside from these, while [i]SVE[/i] tends to offer more numerous & valuable gifts, opportunities, and vendors than in Vanilla, such as free Strawberry Seeds in the mail early on, profitable fishing spots, locations with plentiful valuable forgeables, or shops offering cheap and/or rare items, generally these are noticeable as coming from SVE NPCs or being in special SVE areas, which makes it possible to avoid using them if desired.

[b]However[/b] if you don't use [i]SVE[/i], with permission I have supplied the standalone mod [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/8149]Crafting and Construction from SVE[/url] which just duplicates the effects of the "[b]Balanced Crafting[/b]" and/or "[b]Harder Building Construction[/b]" options from [i]SVE[/i].[/spoiler]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10956][size=4]Predictable Retaining Soil[/size][/url]
Description:
[spoiler]Makes the water-retaining soil fertilizers have a set number of days you won't need to water the tile, instead of being chance-based. A simple change that opens up some interesting new options as it makes these items actually potentially worth using (In vanilla since you'd need to walk around to all the spots that dried out and water them individually, these soil fertilizers wouldn't actually save you any effort). Can configure the amount of days watering isn't needed, e.g. I use 1 day for Basic and 2 days for Quality Retaining Soil, since rain will reset the timer.[/spoiler]

[size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/541]Lookup Anything[/url] & [url=https://github.com/Annosz/UIInfoSuite2/releases][size=4]UI Info Suite 2[/size][/url] or [/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5][size=4]CJB Show Item Sell Price[/size][/url]
Description:
[spoiler]Very handy even without any other mods, being able to see the value of items in your inventory by hovering, or check the stats of a crop / animal at the press of a button is extra useful with this mod as many of those values are different from what you may be used to. 

Notably, using [i]Lookup Anything[/i] on seed packets (even in Pierre's inventory) will allow you to click on the name of the crop itself and see the stats for it without needing the crop itself in your inventory.  [i]UI Info Suite 2[/i] also shows the expected crop sell price directly in Pierre's shop menu when looking at seeds.

In 1.6, [i]UI Info Suite[/i] or [i]CJB Show Item Sell Price[/i] are less necessary for seeing item sell prices as there is a vanilla method to do the same thing, although [i]UI Info Suite 2[/i] also has many other Quality of Life features that can make it very useful.[/spoiler]

[size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/4689]Leveling Adjustments[/url][/size]
Description & [url=https://forums.stardewvalley.net/threads/unofficial-mod-updates.2096/post-129830]unofficial update link[/url]:
[spoiler]This allows you to set your general experience factor to something like 0.5 or 0.33, to make you gain all skill experience 50% or 33% as quickly, which can really help extend the early/mid-game before you unlock all the powerful recipes & abilities. It also makes the choice of what activities to do in the first few days and weeks feel more impactful, as you may have to focus on a particular skill to reach a certain breakpoint you would normally, e.g. getting +1 Forage Berries in time for Salmonberry season. With the way the experience requirements for levelup are set, setting an experience factor of 0.5 would make you be about 1~2 levels below what you would be in a vanilla game on average, still making it manageable to get all skills to lvl 10 before the end of Year 1 (a factor of 0.33 puts you about ~3 levels behind vanilla). While this mod is not technically updated for 1.6 yet, there is an [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/4689?tab=posts#]unofficial update posted on the mod's Posts page[/url] (or a [url=https://forums.stardewvalley.net/threads/unofficial-mod-updates.2096/page-213#post-129830]post with direct link to file here[/url] on the Stardew Valley Forum Unofficial Mod Update list).[/spoiler]
[size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/17055?tab=posts&BH=0]Friendship Tweaks[/url][/size]
Description & [url=https://forums.stardewvalley.net/threads/unofficial-mod-updates.2096/post-130666]unofficial update link[/url]﻿:
[spoiler]This is essentially [i]Leveling Adjustments,[/i] but for friendship gains with NPCs, potentially slowing down how quickly you receive powerful recipes or gifts from NPCs. You can globally increase or decrease the rate at which you gain friendship (and a separate setting for the rate at which you lose friendship, due to not speaking with an NPC for a day, disliked/hated gifts, etc.). The unofficial update also lets you adjust the friendship multipliers gifts have on an NPC's Birthday or as a Secret Winter Star gift. Even a small change such as halving the Birthday / Winter Star / Special gift multipliers (ie setting them to 4 / 2.5 / 1.5) can have a big impact, as in vanilla giving a Birthday gift is equivalent to an entire season of giving as many gifts of that type as possible, which can be a huge amount for a Liked/Loved gift. Doubling the "Decrease Mult" can also make the slow "friendship decay" from not speaking to someone add up a bit faster. While this mod is also not technically updated for 1.6 yet, there is an [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/17055?tab=posts&BH=0]unofficial update posted on the mod's Posts page[/url] (or a [url=https://forums.stardewvalley.net/threads/unofficial-mod-updates.2096/page-217#post-130666]post with direct link to file here[/url] on the Stardew Valley Forum Unofficial Mod Update list).[/spoiler]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1927][size=4]Enhanced Relationships[/size][/url]
Description:
[spoiler]While much less comprehensive than [i]Friendship Tweaks[/i], this can also help indirectly slow down gaining friendship/hearts with village NPCs by causing you to lose friendship each day if you haven't given a gift to that NPC this week. Note that currently by default it will actually increase friendship with affected NPCs, but if you set both "[b]BasicAmount[/b]" and "[b]BirthdayMultiplier[/b]" in [i]config.json[/i] to negative numbers it will slightly reduce your friendship with each NPC every day unless you've already given them a gift that week, scaling down based on how many hearts you have with them already (with the default values each day you lose roughly half the amount of friendship gained by speaking to someone, and more if missing their birthday). The friendship loss (if using negative numbers) will be multiplied by the "Decrease Mult" set in [i]Friendship Tweaks[/i] if using that mod as well.[/spoiler]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/649][size=4]RTGOAT's Longevity[/size][/url]
[i](Now updated for 1.6 and more compatible with Better Balance!)[/i]
Description:
[spoiler][i]Longevity [/i]falls under the "added challenge" category, though I still wouldn't consider it to be unfairly punishing or grindy, and personally always use it.  One of the oldest and best mods aimed specifically at improving balance / extending the life of the game, which I always play with, much like [i]SVE[/i].  Specifically for using alongside this mod, I especially recommend using the [b]Taxes[/b] and [b]Stamina Balance[/b] features, although the [b]Diminishing Returns[/b] and/or [b]Random [/b]& [b]Seasonal Fluctuations [/b]under the [b]Dynamic Pricing[/b] feature (although this will have the side effect of "unbalancing" various prices in certain ways as well) can also add some interesting strategic choices on when to sell things or planting an unexpected crop because the seeds were on sale.

[b]Taxes [/b]will give a set amount needed to pay each month (increasing with the number of buildings, sprinklers, machines, etc. on your farm) as well as a small percentage of your income, starting low and slowly increasing akin to a progressive tax scheme.  This helps by not only providing a "gold sink," but the progressive tax scheme means that it becomes more noticeable the "better" you are doing, and less of an impact if you are playing more relaxed / just starting out, so it never feels overly punishing just for the sake of it.
[b]Stamina Balance[/b] gives slight tweaks & increases to stamina consumption for the various tools, which also helps curtail the "snowballing" of Year 1 by reducing your effective energy, and also scale with your tool upgrade level to still be relevant even later in the game when energy is easier to restore. 

[i]Longevity[/i]'s [b]Dynamic Pricing[/b] is now mostly compatible with [i]Better Balance[/i] (with some caveats) as it works as % increases or reductions to the base values in the game files, which [i]Better Balance[/i] adjusts directly, so any of the Influence numbers you set in its config (if done through the [i]Generic Mod Config Menu[/i] it includes helpful descriptions) work as % multipliers that stack multiplicatively with any Multipliers you set in [i]Better Balance[/i]'s config. Note that the default values set for all the "Base" Influencers were set assuming vanilla prices, so I recommend setting all the "Base" Influencer values to 0 (or all to the same value, like -0.05 for a global -5% reduction) at first if using alongside [i]Better Balance[/i]. [color=#666666][s][b]NOTE[/b]: An exception is for Honey, due to how [i]Longevity's [/i]Dynamic Pricing overwrites the vanilla price formula for honey and thus increases all honey prices in [i]Better Balance[/i]. To counteract this, if using Dynamic Pricing I recommend reducing all Flower values by -25%, either through [i]Longevity [/i]or [i]Better Balance's[/i] config to return the base Honey prices back closer to the [i]Better Balance[/i] defaults.[/s] ([i]No longer necessary as a recent Longevity update changed how Honey price is calculated[/i])[/color]
In particular, hopefully [i]Better Balance[/i] makes most crops competitive enough with each other that the daily [b]Random Fluctuations[/b] feature (even if set to just [b]10%[/b] variation) should be enough to possibly change which seeds you buy at the start of the season, based on if any happen to be on good discount that day. If you only want to use one or two of the Dynamic Pricing features, such as the [b]Diminishing Returns[/b] based on the amount of the same item you've sold recently, or the daily [b]Random Fluctuations[/b], you can just adjust all the other Influence values to 0.

Note that if [b]Dynamic Pricing[/b] is enabled, [b]Diminishing Returns [/b]will also always be enabled which can have 2 unintuitive effects on price balancing:
[list]
[*]Because Diminishing Returns reduces the value of items the more of them you've sold recently, this will cause high-value, low-yield crops/items like Melons/Pumpkins to start outperforming low-value, high-yield items/crops like Blueberries/Cranberries since the fewer of an item you sell, the less Diminishing Returns affects it. Eventually once your farm gets to the point of producing thousands of items per season this effect can go away, since you will likely be hitting the maximum Diminishing Returns threshold on all the items you sell anyways.[/*]
[*]Fruit Tree fruit (and their Wines / Jellies) get "negative" Diminishing Returns in [i]Longevity[/i] where their value increases the more you have sold recently, so if you have more than a few of the same kind of Fruit Tree they will eventually become more profitable than most other options (unless you add the fruit names to [i]Longevity[/i]'s "[b]Price Exceptions[/b]" list, or reduce their base value in [i]Better Balance[/i]'s "[b]pricesBalanced.json[/b]")[/*]
[/list]Also note that currently the [b]Dynamic Honey[/b], [b]Subsidized Crops[/b], and [b]Daily DR Reduction[/b] features only take into account the outdoor portion of your mainland farm, not the Greenhouse or any crops grown outside your starting farm area.
Additionally, the [b]Seasonal Influencer[/b] currently works in a way that will give the boosted "Winter" bonus not just to most crops but also most other items of other categories (and similarly gives the boosted "Out of Winter" bonus not just to Winter crops but also an assortment of items from other categories)
Finally, note that when using Dynamic Pricing, the prices for [b]Dried Mushrooms[/b] (and [b]Smoked Fish[/b] when using [i]Better Balance's[/i] "[b]Smoked Fish are Fish[/b]" config setting) will be unaffected by all Dynamic Pricing modifiers including Diminishing Returns, and potentially [b]Dried Fruit[/b] as well.[/spoiler]
[center][b][size=5]Special Thanks:[/size][/b][/center]

This mod began as a personal project to just rebalance a few of the more egregious things in my own game, but eventually sprawled to balance so many things that I figured I'd offer it for any other users who happen to share my same tastes for game balance, or as a tool for others to do the same on their own.  Especially since I've already relied so much on the efforts & information provided by the Stardew Valley community and modders when playing over the years. 

Big thanks in particular to:

[b]ConcernedApe[/b], for making a game that has brought so many people together.

[b]Pathoschild[/b] for creating the framework for someone like me to make a mod in the first place with Content Patcher, and all the other incredibly useful mods & tools they've made.

[b]FlashShifter [/b]for all the work on Stardew Valley Expanded in general, and making the standalone version of Crafting & Construction from SVE available in particular.

[b]Digus [/b]for the work on Custom Crystalarium Mod, and especially making it so easy to create content packs for it.

Modders such as [b]lech43 [/b]and [b]RTGOAT [/b]for creating balance / challenge oriented mods, despite the game's relaxing reputation.

[b]The entire Stardew Valley modding, Discord, theorycrafting, and playing community [/b]for making so much information such as the wiki or community spreadsheets available to players and creators.
